historical_research_note: Mojang AB (Mojang Studios) is the Stockholm-based developer of Minecraft. Microsoft announced its $2.5 billion acquisition of Mojang in 2014, and Mojang joined Microsoft Studios (now Xbox Game Studios).

Video-game and entertainment business. Revenue paths include sales and licensing of games and digital content, subscriptions, in-game/Marketplace purchases, and distribution through the wider Xbox ecosystem.
Minecraft Realms is a recurring cloud-hosted personal-server subscription. Bedrock plans are listed at $3.99 or $7.99 per month; Java Realms is listed at $7.99 per month.

Minecraft Marketplace sells creator-made digital content through Minecoins. Mojang also operates a creator partner program, and Marketplace Pass/Realms Plus provide subscription access to rotating content.
Minecraft intellectual property: trademarks, game code, art, world formats, proprietary development assets, and the Minecraft brand/franchise.

Player and customer data: names/contact details, email addresses, account credentials, payment data, subscription/license entitlements, purchase history, IP addresses, device identifiers, and connectivity/configuration data.
Account identity and access data: Microsoft account credentials, Xbox gamertags, purchase entitlements, multiplayer permissions, and account security settings.
Player-created content and service data: Realm worlds, saves, backups, in-game content, and social/usage data associated with online play.
Online-service infrastructure: authentication, Realms servers, storage, databases, load balancing, networking, monitoring, and availability systems.

historical_research_note: Marketplace creator content, partner submissions, Minecoin transactions, and the trust/safety processes used to review published content.
Mojang's public company profile describes a partially remote workforce based in Stockholm and Redmond, with additional locations in London, Shanghai, and Tokyo.

Minecraft and Realms operate across PCs, consoles, and mobile devices. Bedrock supports cross-platform play across Windows, Android, iOS, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, Amazon Fire, and Chromebook; Java supports Windows, macOS, and Linux.
A publicly documented 2014 Realms deployment used AWS EC2, EBS, RDS, S3, Elastic Load Balancing, and multiple AWS Regions. Worlds and game state were stored in S3 at that time.

historical_research_note: Minecraft had sold more than 350 million units as of April 2025, according to Guinness World Records, which says the figure was confirmed by Mojang in the official Minecraft Annual 2026.
Microsoft reported that Minecraft reached record monthly active usage and revenue in FY2025 Q4, but it did not publish a current Minecraft-specific monthly-active-user number in that disclosure.

Log4Shell / CVE-2021-44228 affected Minecraft: Java Edition in December 2021. Mojang patched official clients and Microsoft released a fix blocking the issue in Java Edition 1.18.1; self-hosted server operators also had to update or apply mitigations.

In June 2023, malware was distributed through infected Minecraft mods/projects on CurseForge and BukkitDev. This was a third-party mod ecosystem incident, not evidence that Mojang's own network was breached.
Independent security reporting described the 2023 Fractureiser malware as an information stealer spread through compromised Minecraft mods and plugins.

In January 2024, parent company Microsoft disclosed that Midnight Blizzard accessed a small percentage of corporate email accounts after password-spraying a legacy test tenant. Microsoft stated there was no evidence of access to customer environments, production systems, source code, or AI systems.
Minecraft's official website is Minecraft.net. Mojang's official careers page is hosted within Minecraft.net and identifies Mojang AB / Microsoft branding.

Mojang Studios is not separately publicly traded and does not publish its own U.S. Form 10-K. Use parent company Microsoft Corporation's FY2025 Form 10-K for public financial and enterprise-risk disclosures; Microsoft reports gaming within its consolidated business.
SpigotMC's Systems Administration forum contains practitioner discussion of Minecraft server security and Log4j.
Microsoft Q&A contains public discussions of compromised Microsoft/Minecraft accounts and recovery problems.
CISA, FBI, NSA, and international partners published mitigation guidance for Log4Shell and related Log4j vulnerabilities.
NIST's National Vulnerability Database entry for CVE-2021-44228 documents the affected Log4j versions and technical vulnerability record.
